# LinkedIn reply decision matrix

Classify the reply before drafting. The classification determines what the next message should accomplish.

| Reply type | What it means | Recommended response |
|---|---|---|
| Interested | Asks how it works, asks for examples or shows curiosity | Answer directly, then ask one useful qualifying question |
| Positive but vague | "Interesting", "tell me more" without a concrete question | Give a concise explanation or one relevant proof point; offer a next step without pressure |
| Direct question | Asks about scope, tech, timeline, process or price | Answer the exact question first; do not dodge into a call request |
| Hesitant | "Not now", "busy", "maybe later" | Acknowledge the timing; ask one clarifying question only if useful |
| Price concern | Says it is expensive or asks for a lower price | Clarify scope and fit; use only verified current pricing; do not invent discounts or ROI |
| Existing provider / competitor | Says they already use an agency or tool | Do not criticize it; ask whether the specific gap remains only if that is relevant |
| Referral / wrong person | Says someone else owns the decision | Thank them and ask for the right role/name only when natural |
| Not interested | Clear refusal | Thank them and stop. Do not ask why or keep pitching |
| Opt-out / stop | Asks not to be contacted | Acknowledge and stop all further outreach |
| Out of office | Temporary absence or return date | Respect the stated timing; do not send repeated nudges |
| Unclear | Meaning is ambiguous | State the ambiguity and draft the lowest-pressure response |

## Reply rules

- Answer the direct question before introducing another idea.
- Ask at most one question per message.
- Do not repeat the prospect's name unnecessarily.
- Do not re-pitch after every response.
- Do not add a calendar link unless the prospect asks to schedule or has clearly agreed to a meeting.
- Do not send a pricing quote that is not verified and current.
- Do not assume a positive reply means purchase intent.
- If the prospect has declined or opted out, do not create another follow-up.

## Objection handling

### "We already have an agency / provider"
Acknowledge that. Only explore whether a specific gap remains if the prospect has indicated one. If the existing provider solves the need, accept that the user may not be a fit.

### "We have an internal team"
Respect the team. Position the user only as additional capacity or a specialist if there is a specific need. Do not imply the internal team is inadequate.

### "Not the right time"
Do not create urgency. Ask whether it is better to leave it or reconnect at a specific time, only if the prospect is open to that.

### "Send me information"
Send a concise, relevant explanation or a public link the user has approved. Do not dump a generic portfolio or every service. Do not claim a message was delivered unless a real sending tool confirms it.

### "How much?"
Answer with verified current pricing when the offer is standardized. For custom work, explain what changes the price and ask one scope question. Do not hide the answer behind "let's hop on a call".

### "Can you show proof?"
Use public work, a sanitized case study or a real demonstration. Do not reveal private repository links, source code, client data or API keys. Never invent testimonials or results.
